chunks: A shaykh from the people of Qaṭīʿat al-Rabīʿ, from the general populace in Baghdad, from those from whom reports were transmitted, narrated to me, saying:

He said: He said to me, “I have indeed seen one of those from the people of this Household whose excellence they speak of, and I have never seen anyone like him at all in his excellence and his devotion.” So I said to him, “Who was he, and how did you see him?”

He said: “During the days of al-Sindī ibn Shāhak, eighty men of standing, ascribed to goodness, were gathered, and we were admitted to Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar (عليه السلام). Al-Sindī said to us, ‘O people, look at this man. Has any harm happened to him? The people claim that something has been done to him, and they speak much about that. Here is his lodging and his bedding, made spacious for him and not restricted. The Commander of the Faithful intended no evil for him; rather, he is only keeping him until he comes to debate with the Commander of the Faithful. Here he is, sound, and ease has been granted to him in all his affairs. So ask him.’”

He said: “We had no concern except to look at the man, and at his excellence and his bearing. Then Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) said, ‘As for what he mentioned of spaciousness and the like of it, it is as he said; except that I inform you, O group, that I have been given poison in seven dates. Tomorrow I shall turn green, and the day after tomorrow I shall die.’”
He said: “Then I looked at al-Sindī ibn Shāhak, and he was shaking and trembling like a palm frond.”

key_terms.سَبْعِ تَمَرَاتٍ: seven dates through which the poison was administered
key_terms.سَمْتِهِ: his bearing, manner, and dignified appearance
key_terms.مُوَسَّعٌ عَلَيْهِ: that ease and spaciousness had been outwardly provided for him
key_terms.نُسُكِهِ: his devotion and acts of worship

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe Imam Mūsā al-Kāẓim’s knowledge of his martyrdom and the circumstances of his imprisonment?
ai.summary: This narration recounts a witness describing the excellence, devotion, and dignified bearing of Imam Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) while he was imprisoned. It also reports the Imam’s foreknowledge of his poisoning and imminent death, which reflects the chapter’s theme that the Imams know the time of their passing. The report further preserves a historical scene exposing official attempts to conceal wrongdoing against the Imam.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Bashhar who said, ‘A Sheykh from the people of Qatiyya Al Rabi’e, from the generals Muslims at Baghdad, from the ones who was transmitted from (a reliable reporter), said,

‘He said to me, ‘I have seen one<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> whose merits are spoken of, from the People<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> of this Household, so I have not seen the likes of him<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> at all regarding his<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> merits and his<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> (performance of) rituals’. So I said to him, ‘Who, and how did you see him<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>?’

He said, ‘In the days of Al-Sindy Bin Shahak (Vizier of Caliph Haroun Al-Rashid), we gathered eighty men from the perspective linked to the goodness, and we went over to Musa<sup>asws</sup> Bin Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> (in prison). So Al-Sindy said to us, ‘O you all! Look at this man. Has anything new (bad) happened with him<sup>asws</sup>? The people are alleging that he<sup>asws</sup> has been (tortured) with and they are frequenting with regards to that. And this here is his<sup>asws</sup> room, and his<sup>asws</sup> bed, and it is made to be capacious upon him<sup>asws</sup> without constraints, and the commander of the faithful (Caliph Haroun Rashid) does not intend evil with him<sup>asws</sup>, and rather he is being considerate with him<sup>asws</sup>, so that he<sup>asws</sup> would proceed and debate with the commander of the faithful (Caliph Haroun Rashid). And here he<sup>asws</sup> is, in good health, eased upon with regards to the entirety of his<sup>asws</sup> affairs. Therefore, ask him<sup>asws</sup>’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘And we, there weren’t any thoughts for us except for the looking at the man<sup>asws</sup>, and to his<sup>asws</sup> merits and his<sup>asws</sup> ways (mannerisms). So Musa<sup>asws</sup> Bin Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘As for what he (Al-Sindy) has mentioned from the capaciousness and what resembles it, so it is upon what he has mentioned apart from that I<sup>asws</sup> am informing you all, O you number (of people), that I<sup>asws</sup> have been given poison in seven dates, and tomorrow I<sup>asws</sup> shall turn green, and after tomorrow I<sup>asws</sup> shall be passing away’.
He (the narrator) said, ‘I looked at Al-Sindy Bin Shahak, he was trembling and shuddering like a palm tree’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa ibn al-Hassan ibn Muhammad ibn Bashshar has said that a respectable man from Qati‘a al- Rabi‘ (a quarter in the Karkh part of Baghdad) from the general public (non-Shi‘a) of Baghdad, from whom people would narrate hadith has said to me the following.

“I have seen (experienced) from the people of this family of whose virtues people speak, things that I have never seen (experienced) no one else to be like him in his virtue and worship.” The narrator has said that he asked the man. “Who is he? And how did you find him?”

He then said, “In the days of al-Sindi ibn Shahik (a vazir of Harun al-Rashid) we gathered eighty people of the leading personalities in goodness to meet Musa ibn Ja‘far (a.s.) Al-Sindi asked us, “Gentlemen, please examine this man. Has anything happened to him?” People think that he is tortured and they make a huge noise about it. This is his dwelling place and his bed which, has enough room and he is not constrained. Amir al-Mu’minin (Harun al-Rashid) has not done any bad things to him. He is kept here until the right time comes so he can debate Amir al-Mu’minin (Harun al-Rashid). He is quite well and comfortable from all aspects. You may ask him questions.”

The narrator has said, “We had no other intention but to see to the man, to his virtue and his excellent attitude. Musa ibn Ja‘far (a.s.) then said, “Whatever he (al-Sindi) has said about the capacity of the place and other such things are as he has said. However, O people, I let you know that I am being poisoned with seven pieces of dates. Tomorrow my color will turn green and after tomorrow I will die.”
The man has said, “I looked at al-Sindi ibn Shahik. He shivered in terror and shook like the leaves of a branch of palm tree.”
